subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker gating for native and realtime voice input, and what local-storage, provider-egress, threshold, and fallback contract should govern it?
rationale: The feature affects who can trigger voice actions and how sensitive voice profiles or raw audio are stored or sent, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary from the issue text alone.

options.title: Design speaker-gating contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract for enrollment, storage/deletion, provider egress, threshold defaults, fallback behavior, and the native/Gateway/plugin boundary before code.

options.title: Narrow to an extension surface
options.body: If maintainers decide core should stay lean, use this issue to identify the missing plugin/provider API and route actual model-specific speaker verification through a plugin or ClawHub package.

options.title: Defer speaker identification
options.body: Keep existing wake/PTT/Talk behavior and revisit only after custom ASR/native-audio work settles enough to provide a safer shared audio pipeline.

recommendation.title: Design speaker-gating contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract for enrollment, storage/deletion, provider egress, threshold defaults, fallback behavior, and the native/Gateway/plugin boundary before code.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across macOS voice activation, Talk handoff, Gateway Talk/provider configuration, and the product-boundary code paths this decision would touch.
